question.problem: Find the vertex of the elliptic paraboloid $z+4=2(x+2)^{2}+5(y-3)^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
The general equation of an elliptic paraboloid oriented along the $z$-axis with vertex at a point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is 

$$
z-{z}_{0}=\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}.
$$

To find the vertex, we rewrite our equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}z+4 & =2(x+2)^{2}+5(y-3)^{2} \\ z-(-4) & =\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{1/2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{1/5} \\ z-(-4) & =\frac{(x-(-2))^{2}}{1/2}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{1/5}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an elliptic paraboloid that has its vertex at $(-2,3,-4).$
